messages.subject: HMC error
parts:
Hi,

I was testing out the HMC example on the NIMBLE documentation page, and I seem to be getting an error if I try to use `configureHMC()`. If I use `buildHMC()` on the model without using configureHMC first, then it compiles with no problems. I'm not sure if I'm doing something incorrectly, or if there is a bug somewhere. I'm using the current CRAN version of `nimbleHMC`. Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Cheers,

TJ

> config <- configureHMC(model)
===== Monitors ===== thin = 1: beta, intercept, sigma ===== Samplers ===== NUTS sampler (1) - intercept, beta, sigma, ran_eff[1], ran_eff[2], ran_eff[3], ran_eff[4], ran_eff[5], ran_eff[6], ran_eff[7], ran_eff[8], ran_eff[9], ran_eff[10] > ## build the MCMC > built <- buildHMC(config) Error in envRefInferField(x, what, getClass(class(x)), selfEnv) : ‘getNodeNames’ is not a valid field or method name for reference class “MCMCconf”

messages.author: 51531762f4fb63a1
messages.subject: Re: HMC error
parts:
Reprex:

model_code <- nimbleCode({
  # priors
  intercept ~ dnorm(0, sd = 100)
  beta ~ dnorm(0, sd = 100)
  sigma ~ dunif(0, 10)
  # random effects and data  
  for(i in 1:10) {
    # random effects
    ran_eff[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd = sigma)
    for(j in 1:5) {
      # data
      y[i,j] ~ dpois(exp(intercept + beta*X[i,j] + ran_eff[i]))
    }
  }
})
set.seed(123)
X <- matrix(rnorm(50), nrow = 10)
inits <- list(intercept = 0, beta = 0.2, sigma = 0.5)
model <- nimbleModel(model_code, constants = list(X = X), inits = inits,
  calculate = FALSE, buildDerivs = TRUE) # Here is the argument needed for AD.
model$simulate(model$getDependencies('ran_eff'))
model$calculate() # Now the model is fully initialized: all nodes have valid values.
model$setData('y') # Now the model has y marked as data, with values from simulation.
config <- configureHMC(model)
built <- buildHMC(config)

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: HMC error
parts:
TJ, thanks for sending along the reproducible example, and your use of nimble and nimbleHMC.

I think this is a very easy fix, but it does highlight something which could be improved.  Basically:

function: {allowable first argument type} -> {return type}

configureMCMC: {model} -> {MCMC configuration object}
buildMCMC: {model, or MCMC configuration object} -> {executable MCMC}

in slight contrast:

configureHMC: {model} -> {MCMC configuration object}
buildHMC: {model only} -> {executable MCMC}

So, once you have used configureHMC, you subsequently need to use buildMCMC.  However, it does highlight that buildHMC could perhaps be expanded, to also handle an MCMC configuration object as an argument, and function the same as buildMCMC.

Let me know if this doesn't make sense.

Cheers!

messages.subject: Re: HMC error
parts:
Hi Daniel,

Many thanks for the quick reply. That makes sense and has now fixed the problem. Apologies if I hadn't read the documentation correctly, but I had sort-of-assumed that you could swap out the configureMCMC/buildMCMC with configureHMC/buildHMC. I didn't get the MCMC configuration object subtlety. Thanks for the clarification. I needed to add a monitor, hence why I needed to use configureHMC.

It's now running perfectly. Thanks very much.

Cheers,

TJ
